verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_clean_html_unchanged: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Constants are well named (REMOVE_WITH_CONTENT, URL_ATTRS, DANGEROUS_SCHEMES) and there are docstrings. But parse_tag and sanitize_once use single-letter names in core logic (s, i, j, k, p, q, r, e), which caps this at accept.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: There are helpers (normalize, parse_tag, find_close, attr_is_dangerous) and policy constants. But parse_tag is about 55 lines with heavy index juggling, sanitize_once is monolithic with special cases for meta and style, and DANGEROUS_SCHEMES[:-1] depends on tuple order.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Explicit encoding with surrogateescape, newline="", and _cssunescape catches ValueError/OverflowError. However, the scheme check relies on slice position (DANGEROUS_SCHEMES[:-1]), and unterminated tags just fall back to emitting '<'.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: General normalisation (unescape loop, stripping control chars and whitespace, lowercasing, on* prefix) and a deny-list for iframe/object/embed/base/meta refresh. Gaps: <template> and <svg>/<math> are not handled explicitly, and NAME_CHARS would accept a null-split tag name like 'scr\0ipt' as a non-script tag.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: The raw-text scanner keeps quoting, order and whitespace verbatim; the sample diff shows only the dangerous parts removed. But it also drops benign content: every data: URL including inline images, noscript/noframes content, and base tags. The hidden test_clean_html_unchanged failed.
